statement.p: Let h(x)=f(x)\cdot g(x), and k(x)=f(x)/g(x). Use the figures below to find the exact values of the indicated derivatives. All sharp corners in the graphs occur at points whose coordinates are integers or half-integers.

image.shortdescription: graph of a piecewise linear function
graph of a piecewise linear function

p.em: (Enter dne for any answer where the derivative does not exist.)

solution.p: A. From the graphs, we find f(1) = 0, f'(1) \approx 0.667, g(1) \approx 1.333, and g'(1) \approx 1.333. By the product rule, h'(1) = f'(1)\cdot g(1) + f(1)\cdot g'(1) \approx 0.889.
B. Similarly, from the graphs, we find f(-2) = -1, f'(-2) = -4, g(-2) = -1, and g'(-2) = -2. By the quotient rule, k'(-2) = \frac{f'(-2)\cdot g(-2)-f(-2)\cdot g'(-2)}{(g(-2))^2} = 2
